results: 1. Full set of vital signs, oxygen saturation, temperature, and Glasgow Coma Scale assessment
Glasgow Coma Scale on arrival: E1V1M1, improving to E1VTM4 after resuscitation
3. Comprehensive neurologic and cranial-nerve examination, including ocular alignment, extraocular movements, pupils, visual fields, and fundoscopy
cranial nerve examination: limited right eye adduction failing to cross midline, with left abducting nystagmus on left gaze; otherwise normal
mental status / cognitive screen: impaired during acute traumatic encephalopathy
deep tendon reflexes and plantar responses: normal
nystagmus: direction and whether it changes with gaze: no nystagmus
adduction in horizontal gaze (each eye): limited adduction of the RIGHT eye that fails to cross the midline, with abducting nystagmus of the left eye on left gaze - mimics an INO
abducting nystagmus of the fellow eye: absent
skew deviation / alternating cover test: no vertical misalignment
ocular torsion and head tilt: none
pupil size and light reaction: equal and reactive

serum electrolytes, urea and creatinine: normal
serum calcium, magnesium and phosphate: normal
full blood count and biochemistry: normal

dx_raw:
DIAGNOSIS: Traumatic right medial rectus dysfunction—most likely orbital medial rectus contusion or entrapment from an occult medial orbital-wall/facial fracture—causing a pseudo-internuclear ophthalmoplegia

ALTERNATIVE 1: Traumatic partial right oculomotor nerve (medial rectus division) palsy

ALTERNATIVE 2: Occult traumatic lesion of the right medial longitudinal fasciculus causing true internuclear ophthalmoplegia

ALTERNATIVE 3: Transient post-traumatic ocular motor dysfunction related to acute traumatic encephalopathy or epidural haemorrhage
